questions.q: Domaine Huet, one of the two Loire producers the Court names, is the benchmark estate of which Chenin Blanc appellation?
questions.exp: Domaine Huet has made Vouvray since 1928 from three named sites, Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont and Clos du Bourg, farmed biodynamically, in every style from sec through demi-sec to moelleux and pétillant. Montlouis faces Vouvray across the river, Savennières is dry Chenin near Angers and Saumur is known for sparkling wine and Cabernet Franc.

questions.q: A demi-sec Vouvray, its touch of sugar held in check by high acidity, is on the table. Which dish is its natural match?
questions.exp: Off-dry Chenin meets the gentle sweetness of pork and fruit, and lightly spiced dishes, without tasting thin, while its acidity cuts the fat. Oysters want a bone dry white such as Muscadet or a sec Vouvray, a ribeye wants a tannic red, and a chocolate tart would make a demi-sec taste sour, since a wine should be at least as sweet as the dessert.

questions.q: A fruit tart or a slice of foie gras calls for a sweeter Chenin. Which label term, the step above demi-sec, marks that Vouvray?
questions.exp: Vouvray and Montlouis label their still Chenin sec, demi-sec, moelleux or doux, rising in sweetness, and moelleux is the Court's Certified label term for the richly sweet style. Its sugar, kept fresh by Chenin's acidity, suits fruit tarts, foie gras and blue cheese, while a sec goes with river fish and a demi-sec with pork or spice.

questions.q: Quarts de Chaume and Bonnezeaux both stand on slopes above which tributary of the Loire, south of Angers?
questions.exp: The Layon runs north-west through Anjou to join the Loire below Angers, and its autumn morning mists, burnt off by dry afternoons, breed the noble rot behind Coteaux du Layon, Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume, the Loire's only Grand Cru since 2011. The Court names the Layon as its Certified physical feature for the valley.

questions.q: Sancerre growers call one of their soils terres blanches. Which of the Court's two Certified Loire soil terms describes it?
questions.exp: Terres blanches are the pale Kimmeridgian clay and marl, full of tiny fossil oyster shells, on the western slopes of Sancerre around Chavignol, the same seam that underlies Chablis; they give the firmest, longest-lived Sauvignon Blanc. The Court's other Certified soil, silex, is the flint nearer the river and across it at Pouilly-Fumé.

questions.q: The Court's Loire history row points to the grower who made one Savennières estate a world reference for biodynamic farming. Which estate?
questions.exp: Coulée de Serrant, a walled amphitheatre of Chenin Blanc above the Loire with its own appellation inside Savennières, turned to biodynamic farming in the early 1980s and became a reference for the movement across France and beyond. Clos Rougeard is a Saumur-Champigny estate, Clos Naudin is in Vouvray and Château de Tracy in Pouilly-Fumé.

questions.q: Which name does the Court now print for the grape of Muscadet, the variety long known by a Burgundian name?
questions.exp: Melon B is the name the appellation rules use for Muscadet's grape, the B standing for blanc, and the Court prints it with the older Melon de Bourgogne in brackets: the variety came from Burgundy after the hard winter of 1709. Folle Blanche makes Gros Plant du Pays Nantais, Chasselas makes Pouilly-sur-Loire, and Pineau de la Loire is an old name for Chenin Blanc.
